LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.10: Indigenous Kenyan Crafts

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Crafts. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is clay the preferred material for pottery?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe coil techniques in pottery
2. model a vessel using coil method

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFTS
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Indigenous Kenyan Crafts helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFTS
Study Indigenous Kenyan Crafts like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe coil techniques in pottery

What this means
In this part you learn to describe coil techniques in pottery. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe coil techniques in pottery.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Crafts” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe coil techniques in pottery. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Model a vessel using coil method

What this means
In this part you learn to model a vessel using coil method. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: model a vessel using coil method.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Crafts in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can model a vessel using coil method. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Indigenous Kenyan Crafts is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Crafts” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe coil techniques in pottery)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Crafts in your own words. (skill: model a vessel using coil method)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Indigenous Kenyan Crafts to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe coil techniques in pottery.
3. Practise this skill: model a vessel using coil method.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Indigenous Kenyan Crafts from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Indigenous Kenyan Crafts: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Indigenous Kenyan Crafts?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is clay the preferred material for pottery?
2. How is a fabric woven?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Indigenous Kenyan Crafts means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe coil techniques in pottery.
5. Be able to: model a vessel using coil method.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
